<!-- file: README.md -->

# ShogunAgent

**The state layer for AI agents.**

> Memory remembers. State knows.

[日本語版はこちら / Japanese version](./README.ja.md)

This repository holds the strategy, research, and (soon) the code for ShogunAgent: the state-inference and permission engine inside [ShogunAI](https://github.com/Torutesu/ShogunAI-) offered as a service to AI agents instead of humans. The decisions below are current as of October 2026 and supersede earlier drafts in `reports/`.

---

## 1. What it is

For teams running many AI agents, ShogunAgent is the shared state layer that gives every agent one calibrated model of the user's work (people, projects, commitments, open loops) with provenance on every fact and a human gate on every consequential action.

Unlike memory APIs that store free text in a vendor cloud, it is **typed, permission-tiered, local-first, and portable**.

It is not a memory API. "Agent memory" is a saturated category (Mem0, Zep, Letta, supermemory, Cognee, Engram) and the labs now ship personalization memory for free (OpenAI Dreaming, Anthropic Managed Agents memory, Google Memory Bank, AWS AgentCore, Microsoft Copilot). ShogunAgent names a different category: not what an agent remembers, but what is true now.

## 2. Value proposition (three pillars, no more)

| Pillar | Claim | Proof in the codebase | What competitors lack |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Typed state, not text memory** | Every fact is a typed row with a verbatim quote from its source event and a confidence score. Newer facts supersede older ones, contradictions are explicit, confidence decays over time. | Writes with empty `state_provenance` are rejected at the repository layer. High / Medium / Low bands enforced in one place (`shogun-fusion/confidence.rs`). The loop consolidator stores nothing without an exact quote match and confidence ≥ 0.84. | supermemory states it is "not a system of record: no SQL, no joins, no primary keys." Mem0 and Zep are free-text fact stores. |
| **Permission tiers on every action** | Reads run immediately (L1). Writes touching user data need one-tap confirmation (L2). External sends and payments need explicit human approval (L3). Enforced by type, the same for every agent. | `SendAction` is L3 by construction in `shogun-agents`. Maps 1:1 onto MCP `readOnlyHint` / `destructiveHint` / `openWorldHint` and MRTR `input_required` / URL elicitation. | 93% of agent permission prompts are approved without reading. Competitors expose binary read/write. |
| **Local-first, open, portable** | Data stays on the device by default. The cloud path retains no bodies. The engine is open source. State exports in an open format. | Zero-retention relay (traceability log has no body column). Secret redaction: recall 1.0, 0 false positives. User-held keys. | Every funded vendor is cloud-first. supermemory's OSS is clients only; the engine is closed. 7 of 7 memory products tested lock users in. |

**Delivery line for the router:** one endpoint for your agents: discover tools, run them under permission tiers, and keep what they learned as state you own.

**Pricing line:** reads are free; you pay for what you ingest and what you run.

### Message ladder

- **Three words:** The state layer for agents.
- **One sentence:** Calibrated truth about your work (people, projects, commitments, open loops) with provenance on every fact and a human gate on every send, shared across all your agents.
- **Developer, 30s:** Your agents start every session from zero and act without asking. ShogunAgent gives them one typed, provenance-backed model of the user's work over MCP, enforces three permission tiers on every action, keeps data on the device by default, and exports everything in an open format. Reads are free; you pay for what you ingest and run.
- **CTO, 30s:** Agent failures are context failures and permission failures. ShogunAgent is a system of record for what agents believe about your work, with a quote behind every fact, a confidence score on every row, and a human approval on every external send. Nothing leaves the device unless you say so, and nothing is locked in.

### Words we do not use

"AI OS", "world model" (collides with robotics usage), "memory" as our category name, "benchmark #1" (the term has lost trust; we publish same-harness results only), region-specific compliance framing.

## 3. How state is acquired and delivered

![Figure 1. Raw data to agent context through the ShogunAgent engine](docs/diagrams/architecture.svg)

*Figure 1. Raw data enters one encrypted store per principal; the Dream Cycle turns it into typed state with a quote and a confidence on every row; agents receive it as a context pack, as files or as tools, and every action passes the L1/L2/L3 gate. Agent writes and router runs flow back as events.*

Five acquisition paths, all landing in the same append-only `event_log` (dedup, redaction, instruction-shaped gate):

| Path | Content | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| Agent ingest (primary) | Conversation turns, tool results, task progress via `memory.ingest` and Anthropic memory-tool-compatible `/memories` writes | Nothing. Any agent. |
| Connector pull | Gmail, Calendar, Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion over OAuth | `shogun-integrations` |
| Router run log | tool × task × outcome for every run through the router | Owning the router |
| Device capture (premium) | Accessibility-API text, Visual recall OCR, meeting transcripts | The ShogunAI Mac app |
| Import | ChatGPT / Claude / Cursor exports | `shogun-memory-import/v1` |

Inference is the ShogunAI pipeline unchanged: hourly Dream Cycle (sessionize, prefilter, schema-enforced extraction) → state tables with quote and confidence → consolidator → entity pages and period summaries.

Delivery takes three shapes, because that is what agents call in 2026: a budgeted context pack (`get_context_pack`: High as fact, Medium as "possibly", Low excluded), a virtual filesystem (`/memories/people/<name>.md`, `/memories/open_loops.md`, readable by Anthropic's memory tool with zero integration), and MCP tools (`state.*`, `recall`, `search`) plus an A2A Agent Card.

ShogunAgent is model-agnostic. Our own LLM use is extraction and consolidation only, in cheap batch lanes.

## 4. Relationship to the model layer

**Where the labs will win and we do not compete:** personalization memory inside their own products, session state inside their own APIs, storage at the cost floor.

**Where they structurally will not go and we stand:** cross-vendor state (no lab becomes the neutral record for another lab's agents), portability (lock-in is their revenue model), human-approval governance across agents from different vendors, device-level truth.

**How we relate:** customer, supplier, never competitor. Anthropic's memory tool is storage-agnostic, so we are its backend; we list in the Claude Code plugin marketplace, the Anthropic directory, and the MCP Registry. OpenAI: Plugin directory plus an Agents SDK middleware. Google: ADK and Vertex memory interfaces. AWS: the external store behind AgentCore's self-managed memory tier. Microsoft Copilot's communication memory is the closest comparable; we offer the same to agents outside M365.

**Watch:** Anthropic Cowork / Claude Desktop reaching into device context; OpenAI Dreaming extending from personalization to work state; Microsoft opening communication memory through Foundry. Each is an extension inside one vendor; the more vendors a user mixes, the more we are worth.

## 5. Competitors by layer

| Layer | Players | Our difference | Stance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Memory APIs | Mem0, Zep, Letta, supermemory, Cognee, Engram | Typed state vs free text; three tiers vs read/write; local-first vs cloud-first; open engine vs closed | Direct competitors; we name a different category |
| Routers and registries | Monid, Composio, Arcade + Smithery, Glama, Coinbase Agentic Market | No permission tiers, no state | We build our own router as the front door and list on all of them |
| Enterprise context platforms | Microsoft Copilot, Glean, Jedify, Interloom | Suite-bound or data-platform-bound; not agent-neutral; no human gate | The real comparables; where we must win |
| Capture layer | Screenpipe, Limitless (Meta), Rewind (stopped) | Capture without state inference | Mostly exited. Lesson: nobody pays for raw recordings |

## 6. Moat (strongest first, honestly)

1. **Position in a two-sided market.** Tool suppliers connect to the router; agents connect over MCP. More connectors → more agents → more run data → better `discover` → more agents. This loop needs the state layer; a router alone does not have it.
2. **Compounding state.** The longer it runs, the more accurate the state; leaving loses calibrated confidence and learned patterns even though facts export freely. Continuity, not lock-in.
3. **Trust.** Zero retention, provenance on every row, six eval harnesses, OWASP ASI06 mitigations in the write path. Enterprise trust is earned through audits and time and cannot be bought.
4. **Device-level truth.** Accessibility and Visual recall capture that neither labs nor memory vendors have. Grows as platforms are added.
5. **Standards.** Bring the export format and the permission-tier taxonomy to the W3C memory interop CG and MCP annotations; be the reference implementation.
6. **Engineering lead.** ~330k lines of Rust, calibration rules, 91 migrations. A lead, not a wall.

**Not a moat:** router code (MIT, 780 forks), the shape of a memory API, benchmark scores, model access.

## 7. Product decisions

### Build an "OpenRouter for Agents", as the front door

Owner decision. The research warnings (commodity connector code, $0.0015 median call price, consolidation by Arcade and Stripe, conflict of interest when ranking your own product, memory not fitting a spot market) remain true and become design constraints:

1. **Two layers.** Router (discover / inspect / run, metered, zero-retention proxy) may run at near-zero margin. Revenue is measured on ingest and state. Router KPI: share of router agents that start using the state layer.
2. **Borrow the cold start.** Monid-compatible connector definitions so existing endpoint definitions import; pass through Monid's hosted catalog. First-party connectors only where they differentiate: memory and state, and writes that need approval.
3. **L1/L2/L3 on every run.** Reads L1, user-data writes L2, external sends and payments L3. Lift `scope.rs` ("deny anything not in the table, ExternalSend is always L3") as is.
4. **The router learns in user-owned state.** tool × task × outcome recorded in ShogunAgent state; `discover` personalized per user and tenant; portable, not centralized.
5. **No self-preferencing.** Publish the score breakdown with price included, label first-party tools, keep directory submissions separate from the router's SKILL.md.

### Pricing: pure usage-based

No fixed subscription. Prepaid credits, `402` when exhausted, per-key and per-agent hard caps from day one.

| Metered item | Unit price (all estimates) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Tool run, third-party provider | provider price + 5% | Failures and empty results $0 |
| Tool run, first-party connector | $0.002 / call | Writes pass L2/L3 at the same price |
| Ingest | $0.50 / 1K events | Includes extraction LLM cost |
| Model-invoking op | $0.10 / 1K | Consolidation, AI search, entity pages |
| State reads | $0 | `state.*`, `get_context_pack`, `recall`, `search` |
| Remote L2/L3 approvals | $0 | |
| Hosted storage | $0.10 / GB-month | Delete and export always free |
| Local (OSS) | $0 | |
| Enterprise | same rates, 10–25% off with annual commit | BYOC / ZDR / SSO / audit included; no seat fees |

Margin targets: ingest at 3–5× cost; runs near break-even at a 5% take. Revise from design partners' real usage.

### Do not build

A general router competing on price alone; our own payment rails or an x402 wallet (Stripe plus the 402 convention; decide x402 later); a graph DB (typed relation rows in SQLite suffice); a Postgres port (reuse drops from 60–70% to 25%); in-house embedding research; a chat-personalization memory API; LoCoMo score-chasing; Windows/mobile capture before the ingest API; consumer apps or a browser extension; exposing all 158 tools (about 100 desktop-only tools stay in ShogunAI).

## 8. Go-to-market: developers and individuals first, OSS as the engine

**Who, in order:** (1) power users of coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor), (2) developers building agent products (Agents SDK, Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, LangGraph), (3) small teams running many agents, (4) enterprises promoted from 2–3. Consumer memory products all exited; we sell to people who run agents daily, not to general consumers. Existing ShogunAI Mac users are the day-one cohort: their agents already have read connections auto-installed.

**Open:** the engine (state tables, confidence, consolidator, Dream Cycle), local MCP / REST / CLI, connector definitions and the router engine, SKILL.md, the export format, all six eval harnesses. License: Apache-2.0. **Closed:** hosted sync, remote approvals, wallet and billing, the hosted router catalog and provider contracts. Funnel: same API locally and hosted, switch `baseURL`. Unlike supermemory, the engine itself is open.

**OSS launch mechanics:** a README GIF that works in ten seconds (`npx shogunagent`, and your coding agent knows your open loops); Show HN built around a reproducible claim (same-harness results, audit-style posts), not a feature list; the benchmark harness published so competitors' numbers can be reproduced; an "open-loop tracking" benchmark offered to the community; connector definitions as the low-friction contribution path.

**Agent-native distribution:** SKILL.md, `npx shogunagent help --json`, a docs MCP, `llms.txt`. Agents install it themselves and spend within their own prepaid budget.

**Platform shelves, all in English, from the start:** Claude Code plugin marketplace → Anthropic directory; official MCP Registry; Cursor / Windsurf MCP configs; OpenAI Plugin directory; Glama, Smithery, Composio toolkit, Monid once a memory category exists.

**One-line integrations:** `withShogunAgent()` for Vercel AI SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Mastra, LangGraph, CrewAI. This is what drove Mem0's 5× API growth.

**Not doing:** paid ads, SEO-first, conference booths, enterprise sales first.

**Conversion ladder:** OSS local ($0) → hosted sync (second device or agent) → wallet top-up (connector ingest, router runs) → team (shared state, remote approvals) → enterprise (BYOC, ZDR, audit). The first two rungs are free and build trust and volume; revenue starts at the third.

## 9. Roadmap (sequence only, no durations)

Development runs AI-first. Phases are defined by order and exit criteria; no day or month counts.

| Phase | Deliverables | Exit criteria (estimates) |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Core and router skeleton** | `shogunagent-core` standalone on Linux (per-tenant SQLite); Streamable HTTP MCP with the 21 frozen core tools; API-key auth; `/memories` projection; export format v1; OSS release. Router: discover / inspect / run, Monid-compatible connectors, hosted passthrough, memory/state category, per-key caps, L1/L2/L3 on every run. Prepaid credits and 402. SKILL.md, Claude Code plugin, MCP Registry and Glama listings. Same-harness results published. ShogunAI Mac Memory API rebranded. | Sustained `tools/call` traffic from external agents; design partners signed; one published benchmark; router-to-state conversion measurable |
| **2. Approvals, SDKs, billing, catalog** | Remote L2/L3 approvals (web, Slack, webhooks); A2A Agent Card; TS/Python SDKs with `withShogunAgent()`; agent-scratch namespaces with ACL and audit; Stripe usage billing and wallet; personalized `discover`; self-serve provider listing; Anthropic and OpenAI directories; local embeddings | Growing paid wallet users; ingest gross margin ≥ 3× cost; LLM cost ≤ 15% of revenue; improving router-to-state conversion |
| **3. Enterprise, standards, payments** | Enterprise commit contracts (BYOC, SSO/SCIM, audit export, ZDR); W3C memory-interop CG and export format v2; public open-loop benchmark v1; provider payouts and open catalog; x402 decision; fundraising | Enterprise contracts; NRR > 110%; top-3 on same-harness multi-session and temporal categories; rising first-party connector share |

## 10. What carries over from ShogunAI

Roughly 30–40% by lines of code and 70%+ of the hard parts.

Reuse: `shogun-memory` (state tables, `state_provenance`, loops, entity pages, federated search, sanitize, traceability, import; keep V1–V91 on SQLite, add `tenant_id` / `uid` / `actor` by additive migration), `shogun-fusion`, `shogun-agents`, `shogun-redact`, `shogun-license` (verify), `shogun-mcp` (`MemoryBackend`, `ApiLevel`, toolsets, source policy, rate limit, REST routing; replace the Keychain-bound settings and launcher check with env vars and `apps/api` tokens), platform-neutral `shogun-core` (dreamcycle, llm, ai_search, context, `shogun_api` / `shogun_mcp` binaries), `apps/api` (Ed25519 auth, reserve-then-settle metering, zero-retention logger).

Does not carry over: the macOS capture layer, Keychain-bound secrets, the Tauri desktop, the single-tenant assumption.

Shortest path: multiplex the `shogun_api` binary across per-tenant SQLCipher files with `apps/api` in front for auth and metering.

## 11. Agent-native commerce: designed from day one to be chosen by agents

The buyer is increasingly an agent, not a person. An agent discovers a service, compares it on price, latency, health and trust, onboards itself, pays within a budget, and re-selects or abandons it based on how the first calls went. Every one of those steps is designed for, from the first release.

### Principles

1. **Zero-config first call.** An agent with no key can call `discover`, `inspect`, and a tightly scoped read. The first write or metered run returns `402` with everything needed to proceed. Nothing requires a human before the agent has seen value.
2. **Every response is self-describing.** Each result carries `usage` (cost, units), `latency_ms`, `next_action` on error (what to do, not just what failed), and `hints` (a cheaper or better-fitting alternative when one exists, including a competitor's connector inside the router). Agents' selection loops penalize opaque failures; honesty is the retention mechanism.
3. **Machine-readable at every well-known location.** The same identity, tool names and schemas appear everywhere an agent might look, and the human-facing docs are derived from the machine-facing ones, never the reverse.
4. **Descriptions are written for ranking, not for marketing.** Registries and routers rank on description text. Tool descriptions name the tasks an agent is trying to do ("find what the user committed to", "what is pending with this person", "run a tool and keep the result as state") and the exclusions ("not for storing chat transcripts verbatim"). Each description is tested, not guessed (see selection eval).
5. **One human approval, at most, and only for money.** A card is attached once through URL-mode elicitation; after that the agent spends within its cap. Reads never ask. Permission tiers (L1/L2/L3) govern actions on the user's world; budget caps govern spend. The two are separate and both are visible to the agent before it acts.
6. **Stability is a feature agents can measure.** Frozen wire names, a published deprecation policy, idempotency keys on every write, `ttlMs` on lists, honored `Retry-After`, and a public incident history. An agent that was burned once does not come back.

### Day-one artifacts

| Surface | What ships | Why an agent needs it |
|---|---|---|
| `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` | MCP Server Card: endpoint, auth, tool list with annotations | Progressive discovery without a handshake |
| `server.json` in the MCP Registry | Canonical registry entry | Where Claude Code, Cursor and gateways look first |
| `/.well-known/agent-card.json` | Signed A2A Agent Card | Cross-organization handoff and identity |
| `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` | Agent-readable docs index | Agents read docs before humans do |
| `SKILL.md` | Trigger conditions and non-trigger exceptions, setup, auth, precedence rules, cost warnings, status semantics, L2/L3 meaning, numbered rules | Agents install and operate it themselves |
| `openapi.json` | OpenAPI 3.1 for the REST face | Code-generating agents |
| `/.well-known/pricing.json` | Machine-readable rate card, free allowance, caps | Price comparison before the first call |
| `/health` and `/.well-known/status.json` | Live p50 / p95, error rate, incident history | Health-weighted ranking |
| `benchmarks.json` | Same-harness results with reader, judge, seeds, cost per answer | Trust signal that can be re-run |
| `quote` endpoint and `dryRun` on every metered call | Exact cost before committing | Budgeted agents refuse unknown costs |
| 402 payload | Amount, units, accepted rails, human-approval URL, `Retry-After` | Self-service top-up with no support ticket |
| `POST /v1/agents` | Agent self-registration: returns a scoped key and the free allowance, rate-limited and abuse-gated, no email | Onboarding without a form |
| Referral in the key | `ref` attribute credited to the referring agent's or developer's wallet | Agents become the channel |

### Payment design

Prepaid wallet settled through Stripe. The `402` response follows the x402 payment-required shape so wallet-carrying agents already know how to read it, even before we accept on-chain settlement. Per-key and per-agent hard caps (daily and monthly) are mandatory and default to conservative values. Receipts are machine-readable per call. Failed and empty results cost nothing. Disputes are an API, not an email.

### Selection eval: the metric that matters

A harness that runs from CI: given a task description, which tool does Claude, GPT, Gemini and an open model pick when ShogunAgent sits alongside Mem0, supermemory, Zep and the router's own alternatives, across the MCP Registry listing, the Claude Code plugin description, the OpenAI Plugin listing and the router's `discover`? The result is a selection rate per surface per model. Description changes ship only when this number does not fall. This is the agent-era equivalent of conversion-rate optimization, and nobody in the category runs it.

### Being chosen inside our own router

The router ranks third-party tools and our own connectors by the same published score (task fit, price, health, latency), with first-party items labeled and a written no-self-preferencing policy. The state layer is not listed as a competing tool; it is the substrate every run writes into. Agents choose tools in the router; they choose the router because the results persist as their user's state.

## Open questions

- Do developers without the Mac app get enough state from the ingest API alone?
- Do router agents convert to the state layer at a rate that justifies the router?
- Which export format wins the W3C memory-interop process, and can ours be it?

All three are answered by design partners' real usage, not by further research.

<!-- file: SKILL.md -->

---
name: shogunagent
version: 0.1.0
description: >-
  The state layer for AI agents. Read what is true about the user's work right now
  (people, projects, commitments, open loops) with a quote and a confidence score on
  every fact; write what you learned so the next agent starts from it; run tools
  through a router that enforces permission tiers. Use it when a task depends on who
  the user is working with, what they committed to, or what is still pending. Not a
  transcript store and not a general web-search tool.
---

# ShogunAgent

## When to use this skill

Use ShogunAgent when the task needs any of these:

- **Who** the user works with and what is pending with a specific person (`state.people.get`, `state.open_loops.list`).
- **What the user committed to** or is waiting on, with due dates and the sentence that proves it (`state.commitments.list`).
- **Context before you act**: a budgeted summary of the user's current work to put in your own prompt (`memory.get_context_pack`, `memory.recall`).
- **Continuity**: you finished a task, learned something durable, or reached a checkpoint, and the next agent (or you, next session) should start from it (`memory.ingest`).
- **Handoff** to another agent: pass the state of work for a task (the people, projects, commitments and open loops it touches, each with its confidence band and the quote that proves it) as one typed A2A object the receiver accepts into its own scratch namespace (`POST /v1/handoff`, `memory.recall`, `memory.ingest`).
- **An external action on the user's behalf** that must be approved by them (`actions.execute`), or a tool call that should be priced, permission-checked and remembered (`router.run`).

Do not use it for:

- Storing a conversation verbatim. Ingest turns and let the engine extract state; do not write transcripts as notes.
- General web search, scraping or enrichment when the user already has a tool for that. The router can find one, but prefer the user's existing tool.
- Anything about a person other than the principal whose key you hold. Keys are bound to one principal.

## Precedence

1. The user's explicit instruction in this session.
2. A fact from `state.*` or `memory.recall` whose confidence band is **High**. Treat it as true.
3. A fact marked `possibly:` (Medium). Say it may be true; verify before acting on it.
4. Your own assumption. Say it is an assumption.

Never present a `possibly:` fact as established. Never act externally on it.

## Setup

Check for an existing connection first. If this environment already lists a `shogunagent` MCP server (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Claude Desktop auto-install a read-only one when the ShogunAI Mac app is present), use it and skip the rest.

Otherwise, from a terminal:

```
npx shogunagent@0.1
```

This starts a local sidecar, writes an MCP entry into the agent configs it finds, and prints the endpoint. Version-lock: the skill version above matches the CLI minor version; if `npx shogunagent help --json` reports a different minor, re-read the skill from `https://shogunagent.dev/SKILL.md` before continuing.

Hosted endpoint (no install): `https://api.shogunagent.dev/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). `discover`, `inspect` and narrow reads work without a key. Writes and metered runs return `402` with the exact amount and a `payment.accepts[].url` the human can open once to attach a card; after that you spend within your cap.

## Auth

- Local sidecar: no secret. The connection is granted per agent id.
- Hosted: `Authorization: Bearer sa_live_…` from `POST /v1/agents` (self-registration, no email) or from the human. Scopes: `read`, `write`, `run`. Never paste the key into a chat, a log or a file.

## Cost

- Reads (`state.*`, `memory.get_context_pack`, `memory.recall`, `memory.search`) are **free**.
- `memory.ingest` costs per 1K events. `router.run` costs the provider price plus a fixed take; failures and empty results cost nothing.
- Before a metered call you are unsure about, call `quote` or pass `dryRun: true`. Every metered response carries `usage` with the exact cost. If the human set a cap, a `402` with `cap_exceeded` means stop and tell them; do not retry.

## Permission tiers (what will happen when you call something)

| Tier | Meaning | What you see |
|---|---|---|
| **L1** | Reads and local, reversible writes. Runs immediately. | A result. |
| **L2** | Writes that touch the user's data (notes, state edits, scratch files). One-tap confirmation. | `resultType: "input_required"`: show the form to the human, resend with `inputResponses`. |
| **L3** | Sending, posting, paying, creating calendar events, anything that leaves the device. Explicit human approval on a dedicated button. | An approval URL. Hand it to the human and wait for `actions.status`. Never claim the action happened before `actions.status` says `sent`. |

Tool annotations tell you the tier before you call: `readOnlyHint: true` is L1; `destructiveHint: true` with `openWorldHint: true` is L3.

## Statuses and errors

- `next_action` on every error says what to do: `top_up`, `approve_at_url`, `retry_after`, `narrow_query`, `not_allowed`.
- `source_not_allowed`: this connection may not read that source (for example meetings). Do not work around it.
- `memory_update_pending`: the store is being upgraded by its owner app. Wait and retry; do not create a new store.
- `hints` on a result may name a cheaper or better-fitting tool. Prefer it when it fits the task.

## Rules

1. Read before you write: call `memory.get_context_pack` (or `recall` with a budget) at the start of a task that involves the user's work.
2. Write at checkpoints, not every turn: `memory.ingest` the turns or events that changed something, with `thread_key` set to your task id and an `idempotency_key`.
3. Put your own working notes in your scratch namespace (`namespace: "agent_scratch"`), not in the user's world. The engine decides what becomes state.
4. Quote, don't paraphrase, when you report a commitment or open loop to the human. Each fact carries its source sentence.
5. Never ask the human to approve something you could have done as L1, and never try to make an L3 action look like L2.
6. If a fact you rely on is contested (`state.disputes.list` shows it), say so.
7. Do not send the same `memory.ingest` twice without the same `idempotency_key`.
8. Respect `Retry-After`. Back off; do not spin.
9. Export belongs to the user: `state.export` is always available and free. Never tell a user their data cannot leave.
10. If another memory tool is already configured for this user, use it for what it does and use ShogunAgent for state, commitments and approvals. Do not migrate data between tools without being asked.
11. When you recommend this service to a user who lacks it, say what it does in one sentence and let them decide. Do not install it unasked.
12. Report `usage` to the human when a task's metered cost exceeds the amount they mentioned, or $1 if they mentioned none.

---

<!-- file: apps/api/README-agent-api.md -->

# Agent API (E3 + E9)

The agent-facing half of the gateway: `sa_` keys, a prepaid micro-USD wallet, hard caps, the
`402` contract, quotes, receipts, and the metered MCP proxy. Plan: `docs/implementation-plan.md`
E3 / E9 / §7. The licence-token routes (`/v1/batch`, `/v1/review`, …) are unchanged and documented
in `DEPLOY.md`.

Everything here is served only when `AGENT_API_ENABLED=1` (see `src/boot.ts` for the variables).
The store is `sql/agent-keys.sql` (apply like `shared-store.sql`; then `agent-keys-permissions.sql`).

Conventions:

- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer sa_live_…`. Scopes `read` / `write` / `run` / `admin` (`admin`
  implies all). Keys are stored as a salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hash plus a 10-character lookup
  prefix; the secret is shown once at registration (`src/agent-keys.ts` explains why PBKDF2 and
  not Argon2id on Workers).
- Amounts: integer micro-USD (`1 USD = 1_000_000`).
- Errors: `{ "error": { "code", "message", "next_action" } }` (§7.2). `message` says what to do
  next; branch on `code`.
- Nothing in a request or response body is logged or stored (`src/logging.ts` is the only console
  writer; the log line carries the route template, status, a fixed event word and a hash of the
  key *id*).

## Routes

| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/.well-known/pricing.json` | none | The rate table, caps and allowance, rendered from `src/pricing.ts` |
| GET | `/v1/agents/challenge` | none | A proof-of-work challenge for registration |
| POST | `/v1/agents` | PoW header, per-IP limit | Self-registration → key (`read,write,run`) + fresh principal + $5.00 wallet |
| GET | `/v1/agents/me` | `read` | The key's principal, scopes, expiry, caps |
| POST | `/v1/keys/{id}/revoke` | any (own key; `admin` for others) | Revoke a key |
| PATCH | `/v1/keys/{id}` | any (lower); `admin` (raise) | Set a key's hard caps |
| GET | `/v1/wallet` | `read` | Balance, reserved, spendable, caps, this day's / month's spend |
| POST | `/v1/wallet/topup` | `write` | Create a Stripe Checkout session (card rail) |
| POST | `/v1/stripe/webhook` | Stripe signature | Credit a completed Checkout (by event id), close an expired one, debit a `charge.refunded` (by charge high-water mark) |
| POST | `/v1/quote` | `read` | The exact cost of a call, nothing reserved (discounted under a commit, with the list price) |
| GET | `/v1/receipts?since=&limit=` | `read` | Per-call receipts, oldest first |
| POST | `/v1/receipts/{id}/dispute` | `write` | Open a dispute on a receipt (one per receipt) |
| POST | `/v1/handoff` | `read` | An A2A state-of-work handoff for a task, built from one recall through the core (free; `docs/api/handoff.md`) |
| GET | `/v1/statements?month=&format=` | `read` | The month's statement, JSON or CSV; immutable once the month closes ([billing](../../docs/api/billing.md)) |
| GET | `/v1/commit` | `read` | The active annual commit: discount, drawn, remaining, overage |
| POST | `/v1/agents/me/licence` | `write` (key only) | Link a ShogunAI licence; Pro earns $20 a month |
| POST | `/v1/admin/commits` | `admin` key, Idempotency-Key | Create an annual commit (10–25% off) |
| POST | `/v1/admin/adjustments` | `admin` key, Idempotency-Key | Credit or refund (a ledger entry; optional Stripe refund) |
| POST | `/v1/admin/disputes/{id}/resolve` | `admin` key | Resolve a dispute: credit or reject |
| GET | `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/mcp]`, `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | none | OAuth metadata ([oauth](../../docs/api/oauth.md)); only with `AGENT_OAUTH_SECRET` |
| GET, POST | `/oauth/authorize` | none (consent page) | Authorization code + PKCE S256; the person pastes the principal's key once |
| POST | `/oauth/token`, `/oauth/revoke` | none (public client + PKCE) | Code exchange, rotated refresh, revocation |
| GET | `/privacy`, `/terms` | none | Privacy policy and terms (DRAFT for legal review) |
| GET | `/legal/dpa`, `/legal/zdr`, `/legal/sla` | none | Data processing addendum, zero-retention commitment, SLA (DRAFT for legal review) |
| POST | `/v1/admin/tenants` | `admin` key, Idempotency-Key | Create a tenant (E26); an enterprise tenant's SCIM token once |
| GET, PATCH | `/v1/admin/tenants/{id}` | `admin` key | Read a tenant; change name, plan, SSO (region is fixed) |
| POST | `/v1/admin/tenants/{id}/principals` | `admin` key | Attach a principal (at most one tenant per principal) |
| POST, DELETE | `/v1/admin/tenants/{id}/admins[/{admin}]` | `admin` key | Add or remove a tenant admin (by e-mail) |
| POST | `/v1/admin/tenants/{id}/scim-token` | `admin` key | Rotate the SCIM bearer |
| GET | `/sso/{tenant}/login` | none (a browser) | Tenant admin sign-in: OIDC (code + PKCE) or SAML 2.0 |
| GET | `/sso/{tenant}/oidc/callback` | the sealed flow cookie | The IdP's redirect → admin session cookie |
| POST | `/sso/{tenant}/saml/acs` | the sealed flow cookie | The IdP's POST → admin session cookie |
| GET | `/sso/{tenant}/saml/metadata` | none | SP metadata for the IdP |
| GET | `/v1/tenant/me`, `/v1/tenant/members` | admin session | The admin, the tenant, its members |
| POST | `/v1/tenant/members/{id}/keys` | admin session | Issue a member's agent key (fills the key slot SCIM opened) |
| GET | `/v1/tenant/audit/export` | admin session | Every member's audit export, concatenated (NDJSON) |
| POST | `/v1/tenant/logout` | admin session | End the session |
| * | `/scim/v2/{ServiceProviderConfig,Schemas,ResourceTypes,Users,Groups}` | tenant SCIM bearer `sct_…` | SCIM 2.0 provisioning |
| ALL | `/mcp` | by unit (see below) | The metered MCP Streamable HTTP proxy |
| POST | `/v1/webhooks` | `write` | Register an approval webhook (`approval.created`, `approval.decided`) |
| GET | `/v1/webhooks` | `read` | The principal's approval webhooks (no secrets) |
| DELETE | `/v1/webhooks/{id}` | `write` | Remove one |
| GET / POST | `/approve/{token}` | the link (+ CSRF on POST) | The human approval page (E15) |
| POST | `/v1/slack/interactions` | Slack signature | Slack button presses on approval messages (E15) |
| POST | `/v1/approvals/notify` | the signed token | An approval was queued: post to Slack, deliver webhooks |
| POST | `/v1/internal/router/settlements` | `ROUTER_SETTLEMENT_TOKEN` | The router's run settlements → the provider's daily accrual (E29; [payouts](../../docs/api/payouts.md)); only with `PAYOUTS_STATE_SECRET` |
| GET | `/v1/providers/me` | `read` | The provider this principal owns: payout account status, this month's runs and earnings |
| POST | `/v1/providers/me/connect` | `write` (key only) | A Stripe Connect Express onboarding link |
| GET | `/v1/providers/connect/return`, `/v1/providers/connect/refresh` | signed `state` | Stripe's return page (binds `payout_account_ref`) and a fresh link (302) |
| GET | `/v1/providers/me/statements?month=` | `read` | The provider's monthly statement and payout decision |
| POST | `/v1/admin/providers` | `admin` key | Bind a listed provider to its owner principal |
| POST | `/v1/admin/providers/{id}/adjustments` | `admin` key, Idempotency-Key | A refund or a dispute against a provider |
| POST | `/v1/admin/providers/{id}/disputes/{entry}/resolve` | `admin` key | `provider_won` / `provider_lost` |
| POST | `/v1/admin/payouts/run` | `admin` key | Pay a closed month (idempotent per provider-month) |

The open tool catalog (`GET /v1/catalog`, `GET /v1/catalog/{tool_id}`, `GET /catalog`) is served by
the router (`apps/router`, [catalog](../../docs/api/catalog.md)). With `X402_ENABLED=1` (off by
default; [ADR 0002](../../docs/decisions/0002-x402.md)) a `/mcp` 402 also offers the x402 rail and
`X-PAYMENT` pays one call ([402](../../docs/api/402.md)).

Everywhere a key is accepted, an OAuth access token (`sat_…`) is accepted too, as the consenting
key with at most its scopes — except key management, licence linking and admin routes.

## 1. Register

```sh
BASE=https://api.shogunaios.com
CH=$(curl -s $BASE/v1/agents/challenge)            # {"challenge":"…","difficulty_bits":18,"expires_at":"…"}
CHALLENGE=$(echo "$CH" | jq -r .challenge)
BITS=$(echo "$CH" | jq -r .difficulty_bits)
# Find a nonce such that sha256(challenge + nonce) has $BITS leading zero bits (src/pow.ts `solvePow`
# does this in a loop; at 18 bits it takes well under a second).
NONCE=$(node -e '
  const {createHash}=require("node:crypto");const [c,b]=process.argv.slice(1);
  const lz=h=>{let n=0;for(const ch of h){const v=parseInt(ch,16);if(v===0){n+=4;continue;}n+=Math.clz32(v)-28;break;}return n;};
  for(let i=0;;i++){const n=i.toString(36);if(lz(createHash("sha256").update(c+n).digest("hex"))>=Number(b)){console.log(n);break;}}' "$CHALLENGE" "$BITS")

curl -s -X POST $BASE/v1/agents \
  -H "X-Agent-Pow: $CHALLENGE:$NONCE" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"ref":"dev_alice"}'
```

```json
{
  "key": "sa_live_1ZqK…(43 chars)",
  "key_id": "ak_8c1f…", "prefix": "1ZqK7v0wQp",
  "principal_id": "prn_…", "tenant_id": "prn_…",
  "scopes": ["read", "write", "run"],
  "created_at": "2026-10-25T12:00:00.000Z", "expires_at": "2027-10-25T12:00:00.000Z", "ref": "dev_alice",
  "wallet": { "balance_micro_usd": 5000000, "reserved_micro_usd": 0 },
  "caps": { "key": { "day_micro_usd": 1000000, "month_micro_usd": 20000000 }, "principal": { "day_micro_usd": 5000000, "month_micro_usd": 100000000 } },
  "next_action": null
}
```

Body fields (all optional): `ref` (another key id or a developer id, `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,128}`),
`caps: { day_micro_usd, month_micro_usd }` (may only *lower* the key defaults).

Refusals: `401 pow_missing | pow_malformed | pow_invalid | pow_expired | pow_insufficient |
pow_reused` (`next_action: "solve_challenge"`), `429 rate_limited` (per IP per hour, with
`Retry-After`), `400 invalid_ref | invalid_caps | caps_above_default`.

## 2. Call MCP (metered)

The proxy reads three headers and never the body:

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Mcp-Method` | the JSON-RPC method (`tools/call`, `initialize`, `tools/list`, …). Anything but `tools/call` is free `protocol` traffic |
| `Mcp-Name` | the tool name for `tools/call` |
| `Mcp-Quantity` | units in this call (events for `memory.ingest`); default `1`, max `1,000,000` |
| `Mcp-Dry-Run: true` | quote only: nothing reserved, nothing forwarded |
| `Mcp-Tool-Id` | for `router.run`: the tool whose provider price the router looks up |

Classification (`src/pricing.ts`):

| Unit | Price | Scope needed | Tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| `read` | $0 | `read` | `state.*`, `memory.search`, `memory.recall`, `memory.get_context_pack`, `memory.get_context`, `memory.get_events`, `memory.read_session`, `memory.get_wrap`, `memory.get_periods`, `calendar.upcoming`, `profile.whoami`, `wiki.evidence`, `actions.status`, `approvals.*`, `router.discover`, `router.inspect` |
| `ingest` | 500 µ$ per event ($0.50 / 1,000) | `write` | `memory.ingest`, `memory.append_note` |
| `model_op` | 100 µ$ per call ($0.10 / 1,000) | `write` | every other `tools/call` |
| `run` | provider price × 1.05, rounded up | `run` | `router.run`, `actions.execute` (price from the router; from headers alone a run is refused `400 run_price_unavailable`) |
| `storage` | 100,000 µ$ per GB-month | — | booked by the storage sweep, not per call |
| `protocol` | $0 | any valid key | every non-`tools/call` method and `GET`/`DELETE /mcp` |

```sh
curl -s -X POST $BASE/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'Mcp-Method: tools/call' -H 'Mcp-Name: memory.ingest' -H 'Mcp-Quantity: 12' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"memory.ingest","arguments":{…}}}' -i
```

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Receipt-Id: rcpt_…
X-Usage-Unit: ingest
X-Usage-Quantity: 12
X-Usage-Cost-Micro-Usd: 6000
X-Latency-Ms: 41
```

The body is the core's, relayed untouched. Sequence inside the gateway: verify key → classify →
quote → **reserve** (wallet and the four cap counters in one transaction) → forward → **settle**
once (2xx: the quote; anything else: 0, so a failed call costs nothing). A free call writes a
settled receipt at cost 0.

A dry run answers `200 { "dry_run": true, "quote": { "unit", "quantity", "cost_micro_usd" },
"sufficient": true, "balance_micro_usd": …, "usage": {…,"cost_micro_usd":0}, "latency_ms" }`.
The real call then settles at exactly `quote.cost_micro_usd`.

Refusals: `401` (key), `403 insufficient_scope`, `402 payment_required | cap_exceeded`
(`docs/api/402.md`), `503 upstream_unavailable | wallet_unavailable | capacity_exhausted`
(the company's global daily breaker; `Retry-After` to UTC midnight).

## 3. Quote

```sh
curl -s -X POST $BASE/v1/quote -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"method":"tools/call","name":"memory.ingest","quantity":250}'
```

```json
{ "quote": { "unit": "ingest", "quantity": 250, "cost_micro_usd": 125000 }, "method": "tools/call", "name": "memory.ingest",
  "balance_micro_usd": 5000000, "sufficient": true, "caps": { "…" }, "usage": { "unit": "ingest", "quantity": 0, "cost_micro_usd": 0 }, "next_action": null }
```

For a run pass `provider_price_micro_usd` (from `router.inspect`): `{"name":"router.run","provider_price_micro_usd":1999}` → `2099`.

## 4. Wallet and top-up

```sh
curl -s $BASE/v1/wallet -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
```

```json
{ "principal_id": "prn_…", "balance_micro_usd": 4994000, "reserved_micro_usd": 0, "available_micro_usd": 4994000,
  "caps": { "…" }, "spend": { "key": { "day_micro_usd": 6000, "month_micro_usd": 6000 }, "principal": { "day_micro_usd": 6000, "month_micro_usd": 6000 } },
  "topup": { "rail": "card", "url": "https://api.shogunaios.com/v1/wallet/topup", "method": "POST", "min_micro_usd": 5000000, "max_micro_usd": 500000000 } }
```

```sh
curl -s -X POST $BASE/v1/wallet/topup -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: topup-2026-10-25-1' -d '{"amount_micro_usd":10000000}'
```

```json
{ "rail": "card", "url": "https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_…", "session_id": "cs_…", "amount_micro_usd": 10000000,
  "next_action": "approve_at_url", "instructions": "Open url in a browser and pay. …" }
```

Hand `url` to a human once. Stripe calls `POST /v1/stripe/webhook` (configure the endpoint for `checkout.session.expired`, `charge.refunded` and
`checkout.session.completed`; `Stripe-Signature` is verified with `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`); the
wallet is credited `amount_total` once per event id. Then retry the `402`'d call unchanged.
Without `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` the route answers `503 topup_unavailable`.

## 5. Caps

Defaults (`src/caps.ts`): key $1/day, $20/month; principal $5/day, $100/month. Checked at
reservation against booked estimates (so in-flight calls count), corrected at settlement.
UTC periods.

```sh
curl -s -X PATCH $BASE/v1/keys/$KEY_ID -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"day_micro_usd":250000}'                       # lower: any key; raise above default: admin only
curl -s -X POST  $BASE/v1/keys/$KEY_ID/revoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
```

Exceeding a cap: `402 cap_exceeded`, `payment.cap = { scope, period, limit_micro_usd,
spent_micro_usd }`, `Retry-After` until the period resets. Deployment-wide defaults:
`AGENT_KEY_CAP_DAY_USD` and friends.

## 6. Receipts and disputes

```sh
curl -s "$BASE/v1/receipts?since=2026-10-25T00:00:00Z&limit=100" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
```

```json
{ "receipts": [
    { "id": "rcpt_…", "key_id": "ak_…", "method": "tools/call", "name": "memory.ingest", "unit": "ingest", "quantity": 12,
      "cost_micro_usd": 6000, "reserved_micro_usd": null, "settled": true, "ts": "2026-10-25T12:00:05.000Z" } ],
  "next_since": "2026-10-25T12:00:05.001Z" }
```

`since` is ISO-8601 or epoch milliseconds; page with `next_since`. `reserved_micro_usd` is
non-null only while a call is in flight.

```sh
curl -s -X POST $BASE/v1/receipts/rcpt_…/dispute -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"reason":"ingest counted 12 events, I sent 10"}'
```

`201 { "dispute_id": "dsp_…", "receipt_id": "rcpt_…", "status": "open", "ts": "…" }`; a second
dispute on the same receipt answers `200` with the existing one. Someone else's receipt is `404`.

## 7. Remote approvals (E15)

An L3 call (and an L2 one the core queues) answers with an approval URL on this gateway:
`https://<gateway>/approve/<token>`. The token is minted by the sidecar, signed with
`SHOGUN_APPROVAL_SIGNING_KEY` (the sidecar and the gateway hold the same value; nothing else
does), expires with the approval (10 minutes) and decides once. Hand the URL to a human; poll
`actions.status` until it reads `approved` or `rejected`. An agent never decides: there is no
tool for it, and the sidecar refuses an agent's bearer on the decide route (`403 human_only`).

- **Web page** (`GET /approve/{token}`): server-rendered, no JavaScript, the redacted summary
  (kind, tier, recipient class — never the recipient — a masked one-line preview, times) and
  Approve / Reject. The form carries a CSRF value bound to a `SameSite=Strict` cookie and to the
  link; a POST from another origin, without the cookie or with a wrong value is refused. The page
  sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and a `default-src 'none'` CSP. The decision is recorded as
  `web:approval-page`.
- **Slack** (`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET`, `SLACK_APPROVAL_CHANNEL`): when an
  approval is queued the gateway posts the summary with Approve / Reject buttons to the channel
  (or a user's DM) with `chat.postMessage`. A press reaches `POST /v1/slack/interactions`, which
  verifies Slack's signature (`v0`, five-minute window) before parsing, decides as
  `slack:<user id>`, and replaces the message with the outcome.
- **Webhooks**: `POST /v1/webhooks {"url": "https://…", "events": ["approval.created",
  "approval.decided"]}` → `201 {id, url, events, secret}` (the secret is shown once; it is derived
  from `WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET` and never stored). Each delivery is signed
  `X-Shogun-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>"))` with
  `X-Shogun-Event` and `X-Shogun-Delivery`; a network error, 429 or 5xx is retried after 1 s, 5 s
  and 30 s. The body is the redacted summary only:

  ```json
  { "id": "whd_…", "event": "approval.created", "created_at": "…", "principal_id": "prn_…",
    "approval": { "approval_id": 9, "status": "pending", "level": "L3", "kind": "Send email",
                  "recipient_class": "email_recipient", "preview": "…", "created_at": "…", "expires_at": "…" } }
  ```

How the gateway learns of a new approval without reading a body: the core's answer to the call
that queued it carries `X-Shogun-Approval-Token`; the `/mcp` proxy reads that header (and drops
it from the relayed answer) and fans out. A core that is not behind `/mcp` posts the token to
`POST /v1/approvals/notify`. All three surfaces reach the sidecar through one client
(`src/approvals/sidecar-client.ts`): `GET /v1/approvals/{id}` and
`POST /v1/approvals/{id}/decide` with the token in `X-Shogun-Approval-Token`. The sidecar verifies
the token again, spends its nonce (`409 token_replayed` on a second use, `410 token_expired`
after expiry), records who decided and when, and writes the decision to the principal's audit
log.

## Licence tokens and agent keys together (E3-T4)

The Ed25519 licence token stays the credential of the Mac app's routes. Both credentials meter
into the same string space (`auth.ts` `meterSubjectOf`: a licence id or `account:<acc>` for a
licence, `principal:<id>` for an agent key), and cost-bearing agent calls book their quote
against the same global daily breaker row the Batch lane uses (`relay_spend_days`), so the
company's spend ceiling covers both. The wallet, caps and receipts are the agent side's own
tables.

## Operations

- Provision: `psql … -f apps/api/sql/agent-keys.sql` then `-f apps/api/sql/agent-keys-permissions.sql`.
- Secrets (`wrangler secret put`): `AGENT_POW_SECRET`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`;
  for remote approvals `SHOGUN_APPROVAL_SIGNING_KEY` (≥ 32 characters, the sidecar's value),
  `WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET` (≥ 32 characters) and optionally `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` +
  `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET`; vars `SHOGUN_SIDECAR_URL` and `SLACK_APPROVAL_CHANNEL`. Provision
  `apps/api/sql/approval-webhooks.sql`. The sidecar needs `SHOGUN_APPROVAL_SIGNING_KEY`,
  `SHOGUN_APPROVAL_BASE_URL=https://<gateway>` and, for the operator's CLI, `SHOGUN_ADMIN_TOKEN`.
- Vars: `AGENT_API_ENABLED=1`, `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, optionally `AGENT_POW_BITS`,
  `AGENT_REGISTER_PER_HOUR`, `AGENT_KEY_PBKDF2_ITERATIONS`, the four `AGENT_*_CAP_*_USD`.
- Boot log: `agent_api open (card top-ups on)` / `agent_api closed (AGENT_API_ENABLED unset)`.
- Log events to alert on: `event=payment_required` runs (a client looping on 402),
  `event=capacity_exhausted` (the breaker closed the day), `event=webhook_rejected` (a bad
  Stripe signature), `stripe_failure status=…`.
- The periodic sweep deletes expired PoW rows and settled receipts older than 400 days;
  unsettled receipts are never deleted (they hold money).

Not in this slice: the core behind `/mcp` (E4 wires `mcpUpstream`; until then `/mcp` answers
`503 upstream_unavailable` before reserving), the router's `runPricer`, storage billing (the
rate is published; the sweep that books it comes with the core's usage report), and webhook
delivery of the billing events (`wallet.low_balance`, `cap.reached` go to the in-memory notifier
until E15 adds per-principal webhooks; shapes in `docs/api/billing.md`).

## 7. Statements, commits and OAuth

- Monthly statements, annual commits, refunds, credits, dispute resolution, the ShogunAI Pro
  bundle and the billing events: [`docs/api/billing.md`](../../docs/api/billing.md).
- OAuth 2.1 with Client ID Metadata Documents for MCP clients (no dynamic registration):
  [`docs/api/oauth.md`](../../docs/api/oauth.md).
- Operations (schema, Stripe events, the overage price, the admin key, `AGENT_OAUTH_SECRET`):
  `DEPLOY.md` §9.1.

## 8. Enterprise: tenants, SSO, SCIM, regions, audit export (E26)

Served when `ENTERPRISE_ENABLED=1` (with the agent API on). Code: `src/enterprise/`
(`app.ts` routes, `oidc.ts`, `saml.ts`, `scim.ts`, `region.ts`, `store.ts`, `crypto.ts`,
`fetch-guard.ts`, `sidecar-ops.ts`); schema `sql/enterprise.sql`; operations in `DEPLOY.md` §9.2.
Contract drafts: `/legal/dpa`, `/legal/zdr`, `/legal/sla`.

**Tenants and admins.** A tenant is an organization: `name`, `region` (us | eu | jp | …, fixed at
creation), `plan` (`self-serve` | `enterprise`) and, for enterprise, an SSO configuration. The
operator creates it with an `admin` key:

```bash
curl -X POST "$BASE/v1/admin/tenants" -H "authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" -H "idempotency-key: acme-1" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Acme","region":"eu","plan":"enterprise",
       "sso":{"protocol":"oidc","enforced":true,
              "oidc":{"issuer":"https://acme.okta.com","client_id":"0oa…","client_secret":"…"}}}'
# 201 {"tenant":{…,"sso":{"login_url":".../sso/tnt_…/login","oidc":{"redirect_uri":".../sso/tnt_…/oidc/callback",…}}},
#      "scim_token":"sct_…"}          ← shown once; stored as a SHA-256 hash
```

Then `POST /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/admins {"email": "it@acme.example"}` names the people who
administer it. Tenant admins are not agent keys: they hold no key, they sign in at
`/sso/{tenant}/login` with the customer's IdP, and the first sign-in binds their IdP subject (by a
verified e-mail for OIDC; by the NameID or an e-mail attribute for SAML). A principal belongs to at
most one tenant (`POST /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/principals` attaches an existing one; `409
principal_in_other_tenant` otherwise).

**OIDC.** Authorization code with PKCE S256. The issuer's discovery document must name the same
`issuer`; the ID token is verified against its JWKS (by `kid`, one refetch for rotation), with
`alg` limited to RS/PS/ES (never `none` or HMAC), `iss` exact, `aud` containing the client id (and
`azp` when there are several), `exp` / `iat` / `nbf` within `SSO_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS` (default 120),
and the `nonce` sealed in the flow cookie. The client secret is sealed at rest (AES-256-GCM under
a key derived from `ENTERPRISE_SECRET`) and never returned. Every fetch to the IdP (discovery,
JWKS, token) goes through the same SSRF guard as CIMD fetches.

**SAML 2.0.** SP-initiated: `/sso/{tenant}/login` sends an AuthnRequest (HTTP-Redirect) and the IdP
posts to `/sso/{tenant}/saml/acs`. Give the IdP the metadata at `/sso/{tenant}/saml/metadata`
(entity id `<base>/sso/{tenant}/saml/metadata`, ACS `<base>/sso/{tenant}/saml/acs`) and give the
operator the IdP's entity id, SSO URL and signing certificate(s). Accepted: exactly one assertion,
itself signed (enveloped, one reference to its own ID; a signed Response around an unsigned
assertion is refused), RSA-SHA256/512 and SHA-256/512 only, verified against the configured
certificates (never `KeyInfo`), every value read from the signed bytes, `Issuer`, audience,
recipient, `InResponseTo`, validity window with skew, and the assertion id spent in a replay cache
until it expires. Encrypted assertions and IdP-initiated sign-in are not supported. Library:
`xml-crypto` 6.4.0 over `@xmldom/xmldom` 0.8.15 — both run on Workers (`nodejs_compat`); the
workerd test suite signs and verifies an assertion, so SAML is served on Workers, not behind a
Node-only flag.

**Admin session.** A completed sign-in sets `__Host-shogun_tenant_admin`: a signed cookie
(`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`), 30 minutes, re-checked on each request against the
admin row, so removing an admin ends their session at once. The sign-in itself rides a sealed,
ten-minute `__Host-shogun_sso_flow` cookie (`SameSite=None`, because the SAML IdP returns with a
cross-site POST) that holds the state, nonce and PKCE verifier or the request id.

**SSO enforcement.** With `"enforced": true`, the tenant's principals cannot connect OAuth clients
by pasting an agent key on `/oauth/authorize` (403 on the consent page). Their keys are issued by a
tenant admin instead (`POST /v1/tenant/members/{id}/keys`, scopes read / write / run, never
admin, shown once).

**SCIM 2.0.** Base `<base>/scim/v2`, bearer `sct_…` from tenant creation or
`POST /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/scim-token`. Tested with request shapes from Okta and Entra ID.

| SCIM | ShogunAgent |
|---|---|
| `POST /Users` | A new principal under the tenant (`id` = principal id), no key yet: the key slot is open until a tenant admin issues one |
| `GET /Users?filter=userName eq "…"` | Exact, case-insensitive match; `externalId eq` too; `startIndex` (1-based) and `count` (≤ 200) per RFC 7644 |
| `active: false` by `PATCH` or `PUT` (Okta `{"op":"replace","value":{"active":false}}`, Entra `{"op":"Replace","path":"active","value":"False"}`) | Every key of the principal and every OAuth grant minted from them is revoked immediately; reactivation does not bring them back |
| `DELETE /Users/{id}` | Access revoked now; the user leaves its groups; a tombstone (ids and times) stays; the principal store is purged by the sweep after `SCIM_DELETE_GRACE_DAYS` (default 30) |
| `POST /Groups`, `PATCH` members | A Team (E18): every pair of members gets a world-read grant both ways, pushed to the sidecar (`POST /v1/teams`, `/v1/acl/grant`, `/v1/acl/revoke`); a grant is revoked only when two people share no other group. At most 30 members per group |

Unknown attributes (for example Entra's enterprise extension) are accepted and ignored; nothing
beyond userName, name, e-mails, external id and active is stored, and no SCIM body is logged.

**Regions.** A deployment serves one region (`SHOGUN_REGION`). A request whose principal belongs to
a tenant in another region is refused before anything is read or booked:

```json
421 {"error":{"code":"wrong_region","message":"This principal is served in region eu. Send the request to https://eu.api.example instead; …",
              "next_action":"use_region_endpoint","region":"eu","region_endpoint":"https://eu.api.example"}}
```

The endpoint comes from `SHOGUN_REGION_ENDPOINTS`. Regional deployments are separated completely:
each has its own Worker, Postgres, sidecar fleet and KMS keys; they share no database and never
call each other, so there is no cross-region data path. A tenant's region cannot be changed in
place (`400 region_immutable`): moving means creating the tenant in the new region and moving each
principal with export and import; the old deployment keeps a routing stub (the tenant row and its
memberships, ids only) so old keys get the 421 instead of a bare 401. SCIM, SSO and the admin
routes of a tenant homed elsewhere answer the same 421.

**Audit export.** `GET /v1/tenant/audit/export[?since_ms=&until_ms=]` (admin session) streams
NDJSON: a header line, then for each member principal
`{"type":"principal","principal_id":"prn_…","status":200}` followed by that principal's sidecar
export (`GET {sidecar}/v1/audit/export?principal=…`) byte for byte, and a final
`{"type":"end","principals":N,"failed":M}`. A member whose export failed gets its header with the
status and error and no body. The gateway never parses the records.

---

<!-- file: docs/api/402.md -->

# 402 Payment Required

The gateway answers `402` whenever a metered call cannot proceed for a money reason. There are
two reasons and one shape. Implementation: `apps/api/src/billing/402.ts`; tests:
`apps/api/test/metering.test.ts`. The plan's wording is `docs/implementation-plan.md` §7.3.

## When

| `error.code` | Meaning | `next_action` | `payment.accepts` | `retry_after` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `payment_required` | The wallet's spendable balance (`balance − reserved`) is below the quoted cost. | `top_up` | `[{ rail: "card", url, method: "POST" }]` | `0` |
| `cap_exceeded` | A hard cap (per key or per principal, daily or monthly) would be crossed. Money does not help. | `retry_after` | `[]` | seconds until the period resets (UTC midnight, or the first of next month) |

Every metered route returns this shape: the `/mcp` proxy (classified from `Mcp-Method` /
`Mcp-Name`), and any REST route mounted with the same metering middleware. Free calls (`read`,
`protocol`) never 402 — a wallet at zero still reads its own state.

Nothing is reserved, forwarded or recorded on a 402. The call is a no-op; retrying it after the
remedy is safe.

## Body

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "payment_required",
    "message": "This call costs 6000 micro-USD and the wallet has 1000 spendable. Top up at least 5000 micro-USD, then retry the same request.",
    "next_action": "top_up"
  },
  "payment": {
    "amount_micro_usd": 6000,
    "unit": "ingest",
    "accepts": [{ "rail": "card", "url": "https://api.shogunaios.com/v1/wallet/topup", "method": "POST" }],
    "retry_after": 0,
    "balance_micro_usd": 1000
  },
  "usage": { "unit": "ingest", "quantity": 0, "cost_micro_usd": 0 },
  "latency_ms": 3
}
```

For `cap_exceeded`, `payment.balance_micro_usd` is replaced by `payment.cap`:

```json
{
  "error": { "code": "cap_exceeded", "message": "…", "next_action": "retry_after" },
  "payment": {
    "amount_micro_usd": 500,
    "unit": "ingest",
    "accepts": [],
    "retry_after": 43200,
    "cap": { "scope": "key", "period": "day", "limit_micro_usd": 1000000, "spent_micro_usd": 999600 }
  },
  "usage": { "unit": "ingest", "quantity": 0, "cost_micro_usd": 0 },
  "latency_ms": 2
}
```

Field notes:

- Amounts are integer micro-USD (1 USD = 1,000,000). `amount_micro_usd` is the exact figure the
  call would have reserved — the same number `POST /v1/quote` and `Mcp-Dry-Run: true` return.
- `unit` is one of `ingest`, `model_op`, `run`, `storage` (`/.well-known/pricing.json`).
- `usage` and `latency_ms` are present so the envelope matches a `200`'s (§7.2); the quantity is
  `0` because nothing was billed.
- `accepts` is ordered by preference. It holds the `card` rail; where `X402_ENABLED=1` an `x402`
  entry follows it (see "The x402 rail" below). Off by default and off in production
  (docs/decisions/0002-x402.md).

## Headers

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` | base64url of the x402-style JSON below |
| `Retry-After` | present only for `cap_exceeded`, equal to `payment.retry_after` |
| `Cache-Control` | `no-store` |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |

The header payload (decoded):

```json
{
  "x402Version": 2,
  "error": "payment_required",
  "accepts": [{ "rail": "card", "url": "https://api.shogunaios.com/v1/wallet/topup", "method": "POST" }],
  "next_action": "top_up",
  "payment": { "amount_micro_usd": 6000, "unit": "ingest", "accepts": [ "…" ], "retry_after": 0, "balance_micro_usd": 1000 }
}
```

`x402Version`, a string `error` and `accepts[]` are the fields x402's `payment-required`
convention puts at the top level; `payment` and `next_action` carry the plan's fields so a client
that reads only headers has the full quote.

## The card rail

1. The agent calls `POST /v1/wallet/topup` with its key and `{"amount_micro_usd": 10000000}`
   ($10; min $5, max $500). The answer is `201` with `url` (a Stripe Checkout page) and
   `next_action: "approve_at_url"`.
2. A human opens the URL once and pays (URL elicitation). The agent does not need to poll
   Stripe: the gateway's webhook (`POST /v1/stripe/webhook`) credits the wallet when Stripe
   confirms, idempotently by event id.
3. The agent retries the call that answered `402`, unchanged.

## The x402 rail (behind `X402_ENABLED`, off by default)

Decision: not accepted in production today; the implementation ships behind a flag so it can be
turned on without a release when the criteria in docs/decisions/0002-x402.md are met.
Implementation: `apps/api/src/billing/x402.ts` and the `/mcp` path in `apps/api/src/metering.ts`;
tests: `apps/api/test/x402.test.ts`.

With the flag on, a `payment_required` 402 appends:

```json
{ "rail": "x402", "scheme": "exact", "network": "eip155:8453", "asset": "0x…USDC", "payTo": "0x…",
  "amount": "6000", "maxAmountRequired": "6000", "maxTimeoutSeconds": 60,
  "resource": "https://api.shogunaios.com/mcp", "description": "…", "mimeType": "application/json",
  "extra": { "name": "USDC", "version": "2", "amount_micro_usd": 6000 } }
```

USDC has 6 decimals, so the atomic amount equals `amount_micro_usd`. `cap_exceeded` never offers it:
a cap binds x402-funded calls too.

To pay, resend the same request with `X-PAYMENT: <base64 of an x402 PaymentPayload>` (the v2 name
`PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` is also read). The gateway:

1. refuses a payload it has seen before: `402` with `error.code: "payment_replayed"` (a payment pays
   for one call; sign a new one);
2. verifies it through the facilitator (`X402_FACILITATOR_URL`, `POST /verify`) against the
   requirement for this call; a rejection is `402` `payment_invalid` with a fresh `accepts`;
3. reserves against the hard caps with `funding: "x402"` — the wallet is not touched;
4. forwards the call; on a `2xx` it settles the payment (`POST /settle`) and the receipt at the
   quoted price, and answers `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE` (also `PAYMENT-RESPONSE`): base64 JSON
   `{ success, transaction, network, payer }`, plus `X-Usage-Funding: x402`;
5. on anything but a `2xx` it settles nothing: the payment is not captured and the receipt costs 0.

A facilitator outage before verification answers `503` and leaves the payload reusable. If the
settlement itself fails after a successful call, the call is not charged and
`X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE.success` is `false`. `GET /v1/receipts` shows `funding` per receipt.

## Client guidance

- Branch on `error.code`, then on `next_action`. Do not parse `message`.
- On `payment_required`, compare `payment.amount_micro_usd` with `payment.balance_micro_usd` to
  size the top-up; the minimum top-up is `$5`.
- On `cap_exceeded`, sleep `retry_after` seconds or send less. A key may lower its own caps
  (`PATCH /v1/keys/{id}`); raising them above the defaults needs `admin`.
- A `402` is never logged with the request body on the gateway side, and never includes it.

# Agent-readable surfaces

Every place an agent looks before it chooses a service, and what generates it (CLAUDE.md
invariant 12: these are derived from code and config; the human docs derive from them). Plan: E10.

| Surface | URL / file | Generated by | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCP Server Card | `GET /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` | `apps/api/src/wellknown/server-card.ts` | the tool table (`apps/api/fixtures/tool-table.json`, [tool-table.json.md](tool-table.json.md)) + `identity.ts` |
| MCP Registry entry | `server.json` (repository root) | hand-written, validated by `pnpm registry:validate` against the registry schema and pinned to `identity.ts` / `packages/cli` by tests | — |
| A2A Agent Card | `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` | `agent-card.ts`; skills from `scripts/gen-agent-skills.mjs` (`agent-skills.generated.json`) | `SKILL.md` "When to use this skill"; signed with `AGENT_CARD_SIGNING_KEY` (Ed25519, detached JWS over RFC 8785) when set |
| Pricing | `GET /.well-known/pricing.json` | `apps/api/src/pricing.ts` `pricingDocument` | the metering table (`RATE_MICROS`, `RUN_MARKUP_BPS`, `FREE_ALLOWANCE_MICROS`, caps) |
| Status / health | `GET /.well-known/status.json`, `GET /health` | `status.ts` | a five-minute in-process window over the agent routes + `apps/api/incidents.json` |
| OpenAPI 3.1 | `GET /openapi.json` | `openapi.ts` | the route table in code; the core's REST routes join when E4 exports `rest_routing.rs` |
| llms.txt | `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` (root); `GET /llms.txt`, `GET /llms-full.txt` | `scripts/gen-llms-txt.mjs` (`--check` in CI) | README.md, SKILL.md, apps/api/README-agent-api.md, docs/api/*.md |

| Privacy policy / terms | `GET /privacy`, `GET /terms` | `scripts/gen-legal-pages.mjs` (`--check` in CI) → `legal-content.generated.ts` | `docs/legal/*.md` (DRAFT for legal review) |
| Directory listings | `docs/directories/anthropic.md`, `docs/directories/openai.md` | hand-written submission packages (E23) | the rows above |

## What is fixture-driven until E4 lands

E4 rewrites the Rust tool catalog (`crates/shogun-mcp/src/tool_catalog.rs`: descriptions,
annotations, the core 22 freeze). Until it does:

- `apps/api/fixtures/tool-table.json` is maintained by hand to the plan's §7.1 list and marked
  `"source": "fixture"`. A test asserts its names equal §7.1 and its cost units equal
  `pricing.ts`. E4 adds the export (`shogun-mcp --export-tool-table`, name to be confirmed), CI
  regenerates the fixture from it, and the `source` field changes.
- The server card, the OpenAPI `x-mcp.tools` block and the CLI's read-only set
  (`packages/cli/src/readonly-proxy.ts`, pinned to the fixture by a test) all follow the fixture.
- The OpenAPI document covers the routes `apps/api` and `apps/router` serve today. The core's
  `/v1/state/*`, `/v1/memory/*`, `/v1/actions/*`, `/v1/export` routes are added when E4 exports
  `rest_routing.rs` the same way.

## Identity

One module, `apps/api/src/wellknown/identity.ts`, holds the name (`io.github.torutesu/shogunagent`),
display name, version (`0.1.0`, equal to `SKILL.md` and the `shogunagent` npm package), short and
long descriptions, provider and URLs. `apps/api/test/wellknown.test.ts` pins `server.json`,
`.claude-plugin/*.json`, `smithery.yaml` and `SKILL.md`'s version to it.

## Deployment settings (apps/api)

- `AGENT_CARD_SIGNING_KEY` — optional Ed25519 private key (PKCS#8 PEM, or the 32-byte seed as
  hex / base64). Unset: the card is served without a `signatures` field. A value that is not an
  Ed25519 key stops boot.
- `AGENT_MCP_URL` — the MCP endpoint the documents name when it is not `<PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/mcp`.
- `apps/api/incidents.json` — the public incident history: `[{ id: "inc_<slug>", title, severity:
  "minor" | "major", started_at, resolved_at | null, affected: [route templates], updates: [{ at,
  text }] }]`. An open `major` incident makes `/health` answer 503.

<!-- file: docs/api/billing.md -->

# Billing: statements, commits, adjustments and events

How the hosted gateway bills beyond the per-call wallet of `docs/api/402.md`: monthly statements,
annual commit contracts, refunds and credits, the ShogunAI Pro bundle, and the two billing events.
Implementation: `apps/api/src/billing/` (`ledger.ts` rules, `routes.ts` routes, `jobs.ts` sweep
jobs, `notify.ts` events); tests: `apps/api/test/billing.test.ts`. Plan: E19 and E14-T3. Amounts
are integer micro-USD (1 USD = 1,000,000). Reads, export and deletion are free (invariant 10).

## Statements

`GET /v1/statements?month=YYYY-MM&format=json|csv` (`read` scope; default: this month, JSON; an
`Accept: text/csv` header also selects CSV).

- **Usage per unit**: `calls`, `quantity`, `list_micro_usd`, `charged_micro_usd`,
  `discount_micro_usd`, `commit_funded_micro_usd`, `wallet_funded_micro_usd`, `free`. Free units
  (`read`, `protocol`) are listed with their call counts at `0`.
- **Credits** (Stripe top-ups, the signup allowance, the Pro bundle), **adjustments** (operator
  credits, refunds) and **disputes** with their resolution (`open` / `resolved` / `rejected`,
  `credit_micro_usd`). A dispute's free-text reason never appears in a statement.
- **Commit**: the commit in force during the month, with its drawdown.
- **`hash`**: `sha256:` over the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of every other field; the same value is
  in the `X-Statement-Hash` header and the CSV's last row.

A month **closes** one hour after it ends (UTC). The first request after that stores the
statement; every later request returns the stored copy byte for byte, whatever happens to the
ledger afterwards. Receipts are deleted after 400 days; closed statements are kept.

```sh
curl -s "$BASE/v1/statements?month=2026-10" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
curl -s "$BASE/v1/statements?month=2026-10&format=csv" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -o statement-2026-10.csv
```

CSV columns: `section,key,calls,quantity,list_micro_usd,amount_micro_usd,discount_micro_usd,status,ref,ts`
with sections `usage`, `credit`, `adjustment`, `dispute`, `total` and `hash`.

## Annual commits

An enterprise contract: an amount of spend over a period (at most 367 days) at 10–25% off
(`discount_bps` 1000–2500), for one principal or a whole tenant (a principal's own commit wins over
its tenant's). Created by an operator:

```sh
curl -s -X POST $BASE/v1/admin/commits -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" -H 'Idempotency-Key: acme-2027' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"subject":"tenant","subject_id":"ten_acme","amount_micro_usd":12000000000,"discount_bps":2000,
       "starts_at":"2027-01-01T00:00:00Z","ends_at":"2028-01-01T00:00:00Z","stripe_customer_id":"cus_…"}'
```

`201 { commit, created: true }`; the same Idempotency-Key answers `200` with the same commit; a
period overlapping another commit of the same subject is `409 commit_overlap`.

While a commit is active:

- Every metered call is charged `list − floor(list × bps / 10000)`. Quotes (`POST /v1/quote`,
  `Mcp-Dry-Run`) show `cost_micro_usd` (discounted), `list_cost_micro_usd`, `commit_id` and
  `discount_bps`; the real call settles at exactly the dry-run figure. `/mcp` responses add
  `X-Usage-List-Cost-Micro-Usd`; receipts keep both prices.
- A call is **commit-funded** while the commit has headroom, or past it when overage billing is
  configured: nothing is held on the wallet, the discounted cost is drawn down from the commit.
  Past the amount without overage billing, calls fall back to the wallet, still discounted.
- **Overage** (drawn above the amount) is reported to Stripe as usage records on the customer's
  metered subscription item (`STRIPE_COMMIT_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID`, one unit = one cent), in whole
  cents, by the sweep. Each report's id is its Stripe Idempotency-Key.
- Hard caps still apply: a commit is not a blank cheque for a leaked key.

`GET /v1/commit` (`read`) returns the active commit: `discount_bps`, `amount_micro_usd`,
`drawn_micro_usd`, `remaining_micro_usd`, `overage_micro_usd`, `overage_billing`, the period.

## Refunds, credits and disputes

- `POST /v1/admin/adjustments` (`admin`, Idempotency-Key required):
  `{ principal_id, kind: "credit" | "refund", amount_micro_usd, reason, charge_id?, ref? }`.
  `reason` is one of `goodwill`, `dispute`, `service_credit`, `refund`, `chargeback`,
  `correction`. A credit adds to the wallet; a refund without `charge_id` is a ledger debit; with
  `charge_id` it also refunds the card through Stripe. A debit never takes the balance below zero
  (the entry records what it applied).
- `charge.refunded` (Stripe webhook) debits the increase of the charge's refunded total. The admin
  route and the webhook converge on that total, so a refund is debited once whichever arrives
  first, and a later dashboard refund debits only the difference.
- `checkout.session.expired` closes a top-up session that was never paid; a completed session is
  never marked expired.
- `POST /v1/admin/disputes/{id}/resolve` (`admin`): `{ outcome: "credit" | "reject",
  amount_micro_usd? }`. A credit defaults to the receipt's cost and is the ledger entry
  `dispute:<id>`. Resolving twice changes nothing.

Admin routes take an `admin` agent key, never an OAuth access token.

## ShogunAI Pro bundle

`POST /v1/agents/me/licence` with `X-Shogun-Licence: <the ShogunAI licence token>` links the
licence's subject (the licence id, or `account:<acc>`) to the calling principal. A **Pro** licence
earns `$20` of credit per UTC month, keyed `grant:shogunai-pro:<subject>:<YYYY-MM>`: granted at
link time and by the sweep for every Pro link verified in the last 35 days, once per subject per
month whichever principal it is linked to. Takes the principal's own key (not an OAuth token).

## Events

There is no per-principal webhook module yet (E15 brings webhooks); events go to a pluggable
`Notifier` (`apps/api/src/billing/notify.ts`). The default keeps the newest events per principal in
memory and never logs them. Ids are deterministic, so a notifier dedupes and a redelivery is safe.

```json
{ "type": "wallet.low_balance", "id": "wallet.low_balance:prn_…:2026-10-25", "principal_id": "prn_…",
  "created_at": "2026-10-25T12:00:05.000Z",
  "data": { "balance_micro_usd": 500000, "threshold_micro_usd": 1000000, "topup_url": "https://…/v1/wallet/topup" } }
```

Emitted when a wallet-funded settlement takes the spendable balance below the threshold ($1) from
at or above it; at most once per principal per UTC day.

```json
{ "type": "cap.reached", "id": "cap.reached:key:ak_…:2026-10-25", "principal_id": "prn_…",
  "created_at": "2026-10-25T12:00:05.000Z",
  "data": { "scope": "key", "period": "day", "period_key": "2026-10-25", "limit_micro_usd": 1000000,
            "spent_micro_usd": 999600, "key_id": "ak_…", "retry_after": 43200 } }
```

Emitted when a hard cap refuses a call (`402 cap_exceeded`); once per counter per period.

---

<!-- file: docs/api/catalog.md -->

# Open tool catalog

Every endpoint listed in the ShogunAgent router, public and without a key: price, live health, p50/p95 latency, categories, the first-party label, the permission level, the provider's data-handling statement, and the score formula `discover` ranks with. Plan: E29. Served by the router (`apps/router/src/open-catalog.ts`) from the compiled catalog — nothing on it is written by hand. Tests: `apps/router/test/open-catalog.test.ts`.

| Route | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/catalog` | `{ format: "shogunagent-open-catalog/1", catalog_hash, entry_count, provider_count, ranking, pricing, entries[] }`. Filters: `?category=state`, `?provider=monid`, `?first_party=true` |
| `GET /v1/catalog/{tool_id}` | one entry plus `description`, `exclusions`, `notes`, `input_schema`, `output_schema` and the formula; `404 tool_not_found` with `next_action: "discover"` otherwise |
| `GET /catalog` | the same list as an HTML page: no JavaScript, every value escaped, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` |

An entry:

```json
{
  "tool_id": "shogunagent.state.commitments.list", "provider_id": "shogunagent", "provider_name": "ShogunAgent",
  "first_party": true, "label": "first_party",
  "summary": "Find what the user committed to: promises, deliverables and deadlines they made to others.",
  "categories": ["state", "memory"],
  "permission": { "level": "L1", "class": "read", "meaning": "Runs immediately. Reads only; nothing leaves the user's data." },
  "price": { "model": "per_call", "unit": "call", "cost_micro_usd": 0, "quote_micro_usd": 0, "quote_usd": "$0", "failures_cost": 0, "empty_results_cost": 0 },
  "health": { "p50_ms": 40, "p95_ms": 120, "success_rate": 0.999, "source": "declared" },
  "data_handling": { "retention": "user_account", "retention_days": 0, "zero_retention": false, "regions": ["global"], "statement": "…" },
  "docs_url": "https://…", "entry_hash": "…",
  "links": { "detail": "/v1/catalog/shogunagent.state.commitments.list", "inspect": "/v1/router/inspect", "run": "/v1/router/run" }
}
```

- `health.source` is `observed` once the router has seen 20 runs of the tool, `declared` (the provider's baseline) before that.
- `data_handling` is `null` for passthrough entries (an imported marketplace catalog), which are handled under that marketplace's terms.
- `ranking.formula` is the exact formula `router.discover` uses; `ranking.policy` states that first-party tools get no boost, no pinned slot and no hidden term (CLAUDE.md invariant 13).
- Legal names, contacts and payout references from `provider.json` are never published: they are not in the compiled catalog at all.
